name: Question 4
problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=6t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
worked_solution:
First, since $s=6t,$ we have that $t=\frac{s}{6}.$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s\ge 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{6}) \\  & =⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{s}{6}),\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{s}{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Consider the curve r(t)=⟨1−2cos⁡3t,3−2sin⁡3t⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=6t. Find R(s), the parametrization of the curve by its arc length s.

a
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(s2),3−2sin⁡(s2)⟩
b
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(2s),3−2sin⁡(2s)⟩
c
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(3s−6),3−2sin⁡(3s−6)⟩
d
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(s3),3−2sin⁡(s3)⟩
e
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(3s+2),3−2sin⁡(3s+2)⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, since s=6t, we have that t=s6.

The vector function that pametrizes the curve r(t) by its arc length s, with s≥0, is given by R(s)=r(s6)=⟨1−2cos⁡(3⋅s6),3−2sin⁡(3⋅s6)⟩=⟨1−2cos⁡(s2),3−2sin⁡(s2)⟩.
